intro: Most animals who look alone are fine: their parents are close by. When one really is hurt, the kindest thing is a quiet, dark box and a quick call to the people who know what to do.
checked: Contacts checked October 2026 on each organization's own site. Please have a licensed rehabber review this guide before launch.

steps.title: Make sure they need help
steps.body: A feathered baby bird hopping on the ground is usually a fledgling learning to fly, with parents nearby. Baby squirrels and fawns are often left alone for a while too. Watch from a distance. They need help if they're bleeding, can't stand or fly, have no feathers or closed eyes, or were caught by a cat or dog, even without a visible wound.

steps.title: Keep yourself safe
steps.body: Use a towel or gloves. Don't pick up raccoons, skunks, opossums, bats or foxes yourself: they can carry rabies. Call for help and keep people and pets back.

steps.title: Put them in a box
steps.body: Gently place a small bird or animal in a cardboard box with a few small air holes and a soft towel or paper towel on the bottom. Close the lid.

steps.title: Keep things dark, warm and quiet
steps.body: Put the box somewhere quiet, away from pets, kids and noise. Darkness calms them. For a baby, a heating pad on low under half the box lets them move closer or away.

steps.title: No food or water
steps.body: Don't give food or water. The wrong food can make them sick, and baby birds can breathe in water.

steps.title: Call or bring them in
steps.body: In NYC, the Wild Bird Fund takes birds and small mammals every day, no appointment needed. In Jersey City, call Animal Care & Control. Follow what they tell you, and wash your hands afterward.

rehabs.name: Wild Bird Fund
rehabs.note: The city's wildlife hospital, at 565 Columbus Avenue (87th–88th St), Manhattan. Birds and small mammals, open every day 9 AM–7 PM. Walk in, no appointment. After hours, keep them in a quiet box and bring them in the next morning.

rehabs.name: NYC 311 (Animal Care Centers)
rehabs.note: For raccoons, skunks, opossums and bats, which can carry rabies. ACC takes these calls 10 AM–6 PM. In a park, ask 311 for the Urban Park Rangers. From outside the city, call 212-639-9675.

rehabs.name: NY licensed wildlife rehabilitators
rehabs.note: New York State's list of licensed rehabbers, searchable by county and by the animals they care for.

rehabs.name: Jersey City Animal Care & Control
rehabs.note: City-run and staffed around the clock (emergencies only 10 PM–7 AM). 235 Jersey City Boulevard, across from Liberty Science Center.

rehabs.name: The Raptor Trust
rehabs.note: Free care for all wild birds, not just raptors. 1390 White Bridge Road, Millington. Call the infirmary before bringing a bird in.

rehabs.name: NJ licensed wildlife rehabilitators
rehabs.note: New Jersey Fish & Wildlife's locator, to find a licensed rehabber near you for the animal you've found.
